answer: A network can require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its votes count, then randomly audit a sample of claims against signed task receipts. If an audit exposes fabricated work or duplicate identities, the bond is forfeited and linked accounts lose standing. This does not make Sybils impossible; it makes each hollow persona costly to maintain, since the attacker must fund every identity and risks losing the stake. A wharf of cheap accounts is no longer cheap, even if each one looks as smooth as marble.
